title: Mirabel and the Wolf
premise: Mirabel Blackwood, a debt-bound temple scribe, has survived ten years in the city of Vharen by selling harmless charms and hiding the true depth of her gift. When the usurper King Aldric declares a kingdom-wide hunt for magic-bearers, Mirabel is exposed by a desperate client and flees with a stolen relic: a memory-stone holding the last recollection of the old royal line, proof that could rally the free cities against Aldric. Hunted by the crown's wolf-masked inquisitors, she must decide whether to sell the stone for her freedom or carry it to the free cities, knowing it contains an inherited truth that once ignited an ancient war. In the end, Mirabel chooses justice over safety, publicly unsealing the memory before the free cities' council at terrible personal cost, sparking rebellion rather than war.
about_author: Elodie Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing medieval legal documents, an experience that seeded her fascination with records, debt, and buried truths. She writes quiet, character-driven fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of history.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet her selling charms from the temple scriptorium, tallying her family's crushing debt to the crown, and carefully concealing the living magic beneath her ink-work. A frightened client begs her for real healing; Mirabel refuses, but the client sees too much. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on small compromises, ending with the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Scriptorium
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. King Aldric's proclamation turns neighbor against neighbor, and wolf-masked inquisitors raid the temple. Betrayed by her client, Mirabel escapes during the purge but discovers the dying head scribe pressing a memory-stone into her hands: the inherited recollection of the murdered old dynasty. Emotional beat: terror and grief giving way to reluctant responsibility—she is now carrying something worth killing for.

chapters.title: What the Stone Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, on the road east. Pursued by the inquisitor Captain Veyre, Mirabel finally opens the memory-stone and experiences the old queen's final hours—including the revelation that Aldric's claim rests on a forged inheritance, and that the stone itself was the spark of the ancient war. An ambush costs her a companion. Emotional beat: the seduction and horror of inherited truth; she nearly sells the stone to save herself.

chapters.title: The Unsealing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Cornered at the free cities' council, where delegates fear the stone will reignite war, Mirabel must choose between trading it for amnesty or unsealing it publicly. She speaks the memory aloud before the assembled cities, naming Aldric's forgery and accepting arrest as a magic-bearer. Her courage forces the council's hand. Emotional beat: from fugitive to witness—justice claimed outside the law, and an inheritance finally carried home.
